ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows a circle with X as the center, and X to Z and X to Y are two radii; the radius in the figure is labeled 4 in., and the central angle between the two radii is labeled 75°. What is required is the length of the minor arc \widehat{ZY}. According to the arc length formula s = (\theta/360)·2πr, substituting \theta = 75° and r = 4 gives s = (75/360)·2π·4 = 5.23599..., which rounded to the nearest hundredth is 5.24.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a circle centered at X, with radii XZ and XY forming a central angle of 75 degrees. The radius is labeled 4 in. The question asks for the length of arc \widehat{ZY}, so compute the minor arc length using s = (central angle/360)·2πr = (75/360)·2π·4. Evaluate to get about 5.23599, then round to the nearest hundredth: 5.24.
